statuses.text:
Practical example of Brian's wisdom:

I needed a new OG image for @withgraphical's Changelog I pushed this morning.

Instead of drawing it in figma, I made a little tool in our app that I (and my agents, automatically) can now use to make branded images for any URL.

quote.text: Your side projects should be compounding very fast with AI. Every problem solved can be re-used or extracted into a generic module. Every design decision should make the next thing beautiful by default. Your agents should be constantly stealing from your past decisions.

watching @MSchwaibold make some magic over a beautiful bottle of Burgundy.

quote.text:
Ways I like to work and experiment: For this search input component, I can strip away pretty much all of the surrounding UI and focus entirely on the component in isolation.

From there, I can quickly jump between different states, bringing back parts of the UI or the full context to experiment with patterns, behaviors, and interactions.

I don't trust my output when it comes too "easy" ... there's no way I just happened to nail it with iteration #5 

surely it takes at least one mental breakdown to make something great... so I always keep going and even try out the "shitty" ideas for benchmarking
quote.author: raunofreiberg

statuses.text:
oh p.s. this is all in code, so what this video doesn't capture is all the interactions in these iterations as well. 

♻️

I think one of the biggest casualties of AI is patience.*

Developing that virtue is so important as a human, and I can't help but worry that it's becoming so much harder to do so.

*This coming from someone notoriously known for valuing speed and velocity, yet despite all of that I have come to understand the benefits of sticking with it, wrestling with ideas and concepts, and how useful it is to develop this muscle.
Easter eggs ✨

The launch video for @withgraphical is just a compilation of parts of the real product in a single use tool I then screen recorded.

What I love about making videos this way is you can't really cheat: everything you see is real and functional.
